supplierRedFlags.title: Is Your Supplier Legit?
supplierRedFlags.subtitle: Check off anything that applies to a factory or trading company you're considering. These are the same warning signs we screen for before ever recommending a supplier.

personal_account.label: They ask for payment to a personal bank account or personal Alipay/WeChat, not a registered company account
personal_account.explanation: Legitimate factories get paid through a business bank account tied to their registered company name. Payment to a personal account is the single most common pattern in supplier scams — if the deal falls apart, there's no verifiable company to chase.

no_business_license.label: They can't or won't share their business license (营业执照) or company registration details
no_business_license.explanation: Every legally operating factory in China has a business license with a verifiable registration number. A supplier who dodges this request either isn't who they claim to be, or is a trading company posing as a factory.

price_too_good.label: Their quoted price is dramatically lower than every other quote you've received for the same spec
price_too_good.explanation: An outlier-low price is usually a different (lower) spec than you asked for, a bait-and-switch after deposit, or a listing with no real intent to ship. Get the exact spec in writing and compare like-for-like.

no_video_call.label: They refuse a video call or live factory walkthrough when you ask for one
no_video_call.explanation: A real factory has nothing to hide about its production floor. This alone doesn't prove fraud, but combined with any other flag here it's a strong signal to slow down.

pressure_full_payment.label: They pressure you to pay 100% upfront instead of a standard deposit + balance split
pressure_full_payment.explanation: The industry-standard structure is a deposit (commonly 30%) before production and the balance before or at shipment. A supplier insisting on full payment upfront is removing your only leverage if something goes wrong.

no_samples.label: They won't provide a paid sample before you commit to a bulk order
no_samples.explanation: Reputable factories are used to producing paid samples — buyers covering the sample cost and shipping is normal. A flat refusal, especially alongside pressure to skip straight to bulk, is a red flag.

inconsistent_details.label: Company name, address, or bank details are inconsistent across their quote, invoice, and website/listing
inconsistent_details.explanation: Mismatched details across documents is one of the clearest signs of an impersonation scam — a fraudulent party copying a real factory's marketing materials while routing payment elsewhere.

clear.headline: No red flags noted
clear.message: That's a good sign — still worth the basic checks (business license, sample, standard payment terms) before you send a deposit.

stop.headline: Stop before sending any payment
stop.message: At least one of the flags you checked is a serious warning sign on its own. Get a second opinion before you pay a deposit — we can verify this supplier for you at no cost.

caution.headline: A few things worth clarifying first
caution.message: None of these are dealbreakers alone, but get clear answers before you commit — or let us verify the supplier for you.

readinessQuiz.title: Are You Ready to Get a Quote?
readinessQuiz.subtitle: Answer five quick questions and see exactly what to prepare before you talk to a sourcing agent — and what you can already skip.

reference.question: Do you have a product reference — a photo, link, or sample — ready to share?
reference.tip: Send us a photo, a link to a similar product, or a sample. It's the single fastest way to get an accurate quote.

quantity.question: Do you know your target quantity, or at least a rough MOQ range?
quantity.tip: Even a rough range (e.g. "500–1,000 units") lets us quote realistic per-unit pricing — exact MOQs vary a lot by factory.

certifications.question: Do you know which certifications your destination market requires (CE, FCC, FDA, RoHS, etc.)?
certifications.tip: Certification needs depend on your product and destination country. Mention your target market and we'll flag what's required.

budget.question: Do you have a target unit price or budget range in mind?
budget.tip: A target price helps us recommend the right tier of factory instead of showing you options outside your budget.

timeline.question: Do you have a shipping deadline or timeline in mind?
timeline.tip: Even "sometime next quarter" helps us pick between sea, air, and express freight when we quote your shipping cost.

ready.label: Fully ready
ready.message: You've got everything a quote needs — skip straight to the form and we'll respond within 24 hours.

almost.label: Almost ready
almost.message: You're most of the way there. Fill in the gaps below and your quote will come back faster and more accurate.

early.label: Early stage
early.message: That's completely normal this early on — most buyers start here. Try the Smart Match tool above to firm up the basics first.

incotermGuide.title: Which Shipping Term Should You Use?
incotermGuide.subtitle: EXW, FOB, CIF, DAP, DDP — the letters your supplier throws at you decide who pays for what, and who's on the hook if something goes wrong. Answer two questions to find yours.
incotermGuide.step1Question: How much of the shipping process do you want to handle yourself?

step1Options.everything: Everything — I have my own freight forwarder and customs broker
step1Options.destination_side: Just the destination side — I'll clear customs and arrange final delivery myself
step1Options.nothing: Nothing — I want it delivered to my door with as little hassle as possible

incotermGuide.step2DestinationQuestion: Do you want to book the main freight yourself, or have the supplier arrange and insure it to your port?

step2DestinationOptions.supplier_arranges: Let the supplier arrange and insure it

incotermGuide.step2NothingQuestion: Do you want to personally handle import duties and taxes, or have them included in one price?

step2NothingOptions.handle_duties_myself: I'll handle duties and taxes myself

EXW.name: Ex Works (EXW)
EXW.summary: The supplier just makes the goods available at their factory — you or your agent handle everything from there.
EXW.watchOut: You're on the hook for export customs paperwork too, which most overseas buyers aren't set up to file themselves — usually only worth it if you already have a China-based agent.

FOB.name: Free On Board (FOB)
FOB.summary: The supplier delivers the goods onto the ship and clears export customs — you take over from the port of departure.
FOB.watchOut: The most common choice for experienced importers who want to shop around for their own freight forwarder and control shipping cost directly.

CIF.name: Cost, Insurance & Freight (CIF)
CIF.summary: The supplier arranges and pays for the main freight and insurance to your destination port — you take over from there.
CIF.watchOut: Convenient, but the supplier picks the carrier and insurer, which sometimes costs more than booking it yourself would.

DAP.name: Delivered At Place (DAP)
DAP.summary: The supplier delivers all the way to your named destination — but you're still responsible for import customs clearance and paying duties/taxes.
DAP.watchOut: Unexpected duty and tax bills right when the shipment arrives are the most common surprise here — ask for an estimate up front.

DDP.name: Delivered Duty Paid (DDP)
DDP.summary: The supplier handles everything, including import duties and taxes — you just receive the delivery.
DDP.watchOut: The simplest option, but usually the most expensive per unit since the supplier is pricing in every risk and fee upfront.

orderTiming.title: Will Your Order Beat the Holidays?
orderTiming.subtitle: Chinese New Year, Golden Week, and peak shipping season quietly add weeks to a timeline that looks fine on paper. Check your target delivery date against them.
orderTiming.targetDateLabel: When do you need it delivered?
orderTiming.leadTimeHint: Typical: ~20-25 days air, ~35-45 days sea. Add 10-15 for custom production.
orderTiming.noClosures: No factory closures fall inside this window.
orderTiming.closureOverlapOne: Your window overlaps a factory closure — {days} closure day added to stay on schedule.
orderTiming.closureOverlapMany: Your window overlaps a factory closure — {days} closure days added to stay on schedule.

cny.name: Chinese New Year {year}
cny.note: Most factories close for one to two weeks around Chinese New Year and take another one to two weeks to return to full output — the single biggest cause of missed deadlines in China sourcing.

peakSeason.name: Peak shipping season {year}
peakSeason.note: Freight rates rise and container space tightens as factories rush to ship before Christmas retail deadlines — book earlier than usual and expect less flexibility on price.

goldenWeek.name: Golden Week {year}
goldenWeek.note: China's National Day holiday — factories and customs offices close for about a week nationwide.

laborDay.name: Labor Day holiday {year}
laborDay.note: A shorter nationwide holiday, but it still closes factories and can add a few days to a production timeline.

paymentSchedule.escrowTip: Consider routing the deposit through a Trade Assurance or escrow-style payment instead of a direct wire — it holds your payment until the supplier ships what was agreed.

deposit.note: {pct}% deposit to confirm your order and start production.

productionStart.label: Production starts

balance.label: Balance due
balance.note: Remaining balance, due before the goods are released for shipment.

ship.label: Goods ship

planMatch.q2: Do you need custom branding, private labeling, or product development on top of sourcing?

documentChecklist.title: What Documents Will You Need?
documentChecklist.subtitle: Pick your product category and get the paperwork checklist for a China shipment — the same documents we prepare for every order.
documentChecklist.disclaimer: A general starting list, not a substitute for your customs broker's guidance — exact requirements vary by destination country and change over time.

commercialInvoice.name: Commercial Invoice
commercialInvoice.note: Lists what's being shipped and its declared value — customs uses this to assess duty.

packingList.name: Packing List
packingList.note: Itemizes what's in each carton — customs and your freight forwarder both need this to match cargo to paperwork.

billOfLading.name: Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air)
billOfLading.note: Your proof of shipment, and the document that lets you or your forwarder claim the goods at destination.

certOfOrigin.name: Certificate of Origin
certOfOrigin.note: States the goods were manufactured in China — sometimes required for preferential duty rates depending on your country's trade agreements.
